name: Daily Reading Habits (Consistency)

objectives.text: Identify the Bible as God's Word that families and classes read together every day
Follow a simple daily class Bible time by opening the Bible, listening quietly to a passage, and praying afterward
Name times and places in an ordinary day when a family or student can read the Bible, using the examples in Deuteronomy 6
Explain why Scripture compares God's Word to the daily food people need to live
Use a simple chart to record daily Bible reading or listening across a full week
Describe examples in Scripture of people who read or heard God's Word as a regular custom, such as Jesus in the synagogue and the Bereans
Compare forming a Bible reading habit with forming other daily habits and identify what helps a habit last, such as a set time, place, and reminder
Explain what the commands to the king and to Joshua teach about reading God's law regularly throughout life
Maintain a reading log that records the date, passage, and one key sentence for each daily reading over several weeks
Analyze a personal weekly schedule to identify obstacles to consistent Bible reading and propose specific adjustments
Explain the Reformed teaching that all people are bound to read Scripture both by themselves and with their families
Explain how Jesus' teaching about abiding in him and his words has been used to ground the practice of regular Scripture reading
Design a short routine for beginning and ending daily reading that applies the catechism's call to diligence, preparation, and prayer
Evaluate different times of day, settings, and formats such as print or audio for how well they support focused and consistent reading
Distinguish between daily Scripture reading as an ordinary means of grace and reading as an attempt to earn God's favor
Explain the historic Reformed practice of daily family worship and the place of Scripture reading within it
Analyze common causes of inconsistent reading and evaluate practical strategies for resuming the habit after missed days
Write an argument defending the priority of regular Scripture reading against the pressure of busyness using Scripture and the confessions
Create a sustainable personal rhythm for daily Scripture reading for life after graduation that plans for changing schedules and includes accountability
Lead a younger class or peer group through a consistent daily reading routine over a set period

changes: Kept and reworded real competencies (daily reading at K, times of day, food imagery, tracking chart, habit comparison, schedule analysis, abiding, time-of-day evaluation, inconsistency strategies, defending against busyness). Dropped imitation of posture and asking for stories as non-assessable, the information versus transformation item (belongs to Reading for Devotion), the whole-Bible plan (belongs to Whole-Bible Reading Plans), and the vague synthesis objective. Added biblical examples of regular reading, king and Joshua commands, reading log, WLC Q156 duty to read, WSC Q90 preparation routine, means of grace versus earning favor, family worship (WCF 21.6), and leading a reading routine. Added catechism and confession anchors where they state the doctrine.
